subject: Linguistics
title: The Spread of Writing
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Spread of Writing.

hook.text: Most writing systems in the world today descend from a single invention—the Phoenician alphabet.

buildup.text: Writing spread through trade, conquest, and missionary activity across continents.

discovery.text: Phoenician begat Greek, which begat Latin and Cyrillic. Aramaic begat Arabic and Hebrew scripts.

twist.text: Some scripts were created by individuals: Cherokee, Korean Hangul, and Vai were designed by named inventors.

climax.text: Writing's spread shows how one innovation can reshape civilization across millennia.

punchline.text: One Phoenician idea became half the world's scripts.

quiz.question: Which ancient script is the ancestor of most modern alphabets?
